units: 1 unit = 1 metre, Y up, models face +Z, pivots at the base. Roads and terrain are generated meshes described by this file, not placed props.

reference.note: Redesigned against Nintendo Switch Pokemon maps after the first attempt was rejected. Screens studied are listed in Tools/Level/reference/SOURCES.md.
principles: A road is one continuous ribbon with a worn edge, never a field of tiles.
The walkable band is 3-5x the road width, and the space either side of the road is mostly empty grass -- density lives at the corridor edges.
Corridor edges are massed: overlapping tree clusters and cliff feet, never evenly spaced individuals.
Terrain gates progress -- a river with one bridge, a one-way ledge, a gorge that pinches -- rather than invisible walls.
Tall grass is a contiguous field with a hard silhouette, adjacent to the road, and it is avoidable.
A town has one street with a hierarchy off it; every building addresses the street from a bounded plot; the landmark is staged at the head.

extents.note: 122 x 120 m. Smaller than the rejected layout on purpose.

layerContract.note: There is no 'Foliage' layer in this project. Terrain, cliffs, foliage and town geometry go on Environment; the generated terrain and road meshes on Ground; props the player can talk to on Interactable; zone/grass/water triggers on ZoneTrigger.

camera.kind: fixed three-quarter; follows the player, never orbits
camera.note: Yaw is fixed at 45 deg, so the camera always sits south-west of the player. Any surface the player can stand in front of is only legible if it faces roughly south-west, which is why the lab, the cave mouth and every shop front in this layout face that way, and why the route is authored so the player walks north-east into the screen. At 38 deg and 5.5 m the camera is 3.39 m up and 4.33 m back and a screenful of ground is about 14 m -- so every 14 m of road gets its own picture.

depthOfField.note: DOF needs something at each depth. The composition rule used throughout is three layers per shot: a near framing element 1.5-3.5 m off the road edge (bush, boulder, fern, fence post, lamp), the sharp midground the player walks in, and a far silhouette (cliff tier, ridge, lab dome, tree wall) beyond 22 m. The road corridor is kept empty in between -- that gap IS the composition.

terrain.note: One continuous surface, not decks. Sample it with heightField.grid (bilinear) or re-evaluate the composition below -- every Y in this file was read from the grid, so both agree.

heightField.composition: y = regionalBase + sum(masses) + streamChannel + pathConform + microRelief
heightField.massRule: each mass adds amount * smootherstep(1 - d/shoulder) where d is the signed distance to its polygon, clamped to [0, shoulder]; smootherstep(t) = t^3(6t^2 - 15t + 10)
heightField.pathConformRule: inside width/2 the terrain is set to the road's own elevation, then feathered to the natural surface over edgeBlend + 0.7 m; suppressed inside conformExclusions

masses.name: Mass_SouthHills
masses.note: Hills closing the map to the south. The polygon itself sits outside the extents, so only the rising shoulder is ever in frame -- a hill you can see the top of stops being a boundary and starts being a place you want to go. Pushed 12-15 m south of where it was west of x=8, which is what gave the enlarged town its southern plots. The two vertices east of x=8 are the originals, so the stream valley's south wall has not moved.

masses.name: Mass_WestHills
masses.note: Western boundary. Same trick: the flat top is off-map. Pushed 9 m west south of z=-8 to open the town's west quarter; (-43.17, -2) is the point the old edge passed through, so everything from z=-2 north -- which is the Field scene's west wall -- is unchanged to the millimetre.

masses.name: Mass_TownPlateau
masses.note: Aster Town sits 2.4 m above the valley on a natural terrace. The 1.1 m shoulder makes the north and east edges a retaining cliff you can see from the route; the south and west edges are swallowed by the hills instead. The whole north-east arc from (4,-22) round to (-30,2) is untouched -- the rim cliff, the gate ramp, the town-rim ledge and the scene seam all hang off it. The south and west run *under* the hills rather than stopping short of them: a terrace that ends before the hillside starts leaves a two-metre ditch at the town's own foot that nothing can reach.

masses.name: Mass_LabForecourt
masses.note: The lab stands one 0.4 m step above the plaza. Staging, and it is inside the 0.45 m step limit so it needs no stairs.

masses.name: Mass_ValleyDish
masses.note: The route floor is a shallow dish, not a plane. Gives the road a crown.

masses.name: Mass_LowerShelf
masses.note: The shelf below the route's one-way ledge. Holds a tall-grass field and an item; you hop down into it and have to walk back around.

masses.name: Mass_TownRimStep
masses.note: Intermediate step at the foot of the town cliff. Turns an unhoppable 2.4 m drop into two 1.2 m hops -- the classic double ledge shortcut out of town.

masses.name: Mass_MassifWest
masses.note: The massif that walls the route's north side and contains the cave. Its eastern face and the spur's western face form the gorge between them.

masses.name: Mass_MassifSpur
masses.note: East spur. Its south face carries the waterfall that feeds the stream, and it is the far silhouette in every shot looking up the route.

masses.name: Mass_CaveApron
masses.note: The bench at the head of the gorge that the cave mouth opens onto.

masses.name: Mass_LakeBowl
masses.note: The lake sits in a real bowl. The 14 m shoulder is what produces a beach you can walk down instead of a wall of water.

masses.name: Mass_MassifCrest
masses.note: Domes the massif's top from 13 m to 20 m. Without this the plateau reads as a table; every Legends: Arceus hillside has a crest line.

masses.name: Mass_SpurCrest
masses.note: Same for the east spur, and it puts the waterfall's catchment above its lip.

masses.name: Mass_RidgeBackdrop
masses.note: Far skyline beyond the lake. Never walkable; exists so the background DOF layer has a silhouette to blur.

masses.name: Mass_EastHills
masses.note: Closes the map east and south-east of the lake without a hard wall, and meets Mass_SouthEastHills so there is no flat leftover between them.

masses.name: Mass_SouthEastHills
masses.note: Rises behind the stream valley in the south-east. The stream and its riparian trees run across its foot, so the quarter of the map the player never walks in is still a view rather than a blank lawn. Its west edge was brought 8 m closer to the town below z=-24: everything between the town's east rim and x=20 was a dead flat at 0.0-0.3 m, which is what you saw over the rim from inside the town -- the map running out. It is now a hillside that closes the view. North of z=-14 the polygon is unchanged, so the stream valley and the crossroads are untouched.

surfacePatches.name: Patch_CentreForecourt
surfacePatches.note: The Centre's forecourt, run into the plaza's north edge so the two read as one paved surface.

surfacePatches.name: Patch_TownYard
surfacePatches.note: The working yard behind the south row: cart, trough and stock. The one piece of the town that is not a garden.

surfacePatches.name: Patch_Plaza
surfacePatches.note: The plaza is a widening of the main street, not a separate square. Aster Town has one paved surface and it changes width.

surfacePatches.name: Patch_Crossroads
surfacePatches.note: The junction is a worn clearing, which is what a real fork looks like -- the road widens where feet mill about.

cliffs.name: Cliff_TownPlateau
cliffs.note: Generate a skirt between topPolyline and basePolyline. The height field already produces this face at 1.1 m of shoulder (65 deg); this entry exists so it can be given rock material and a hard normal break instead of being smoothed into the grass.

cliffs.name: Cliff_LowerShelf
cliffs.note: Generate a skirt between topPolyline and basePolyline. The height field already produces this face at 1.0 m of shoulder (53 deg); this entry exists so it can be given rock material and a hard normal break instead of being smoothed into the grass.

cliffs.name: Cliff_TownRimStep
cliffs.note: Generate a skirt between topPolyline and basePolyline. The height field already produces this face at 1.0 m of shoulder (49 deg); this entry exists so it can be given rock material and a hard normal break instead of being smoothed into the grass.

cliffs.name: Cliff_MassifWest
cliffs.note: Generate a skirt between topPolyline and basePolyline. The height field already produces this face at 1.5 m of shoulder (83 deg); this entry exists so it can be given rock material and a hard normal break instead of being smoothed into the grass.

cliffs.name: Cliff_MassifSpur
cliffs.note: Generate a skirt between topPolyline and basePolyline. The height field already produces this face at 1.5 m of shoulder (81 deg); this entry exists so it can be given rock material and a hard normal break instead of being smoothed into the grass.

ramps.name: Ramp_TownGate
ramps.note: The cut through the town's retaining cliff.

ramps.name: Ramp_Gorge
ramps.note: Steepest stretch of the gorge climb.

ramps.name: Ramp_LakeDescent
ramps.note: Drops the road into the lake basin.

ramps.name: Ramp_LabForecourt
ramps.note: 0.4 m step up to the lab. Inside PlayerLocomotion's 0.45 m step limit, so it needs no stair geometry.

ledges.name: Ledge_Route_South
ledges.note: Hop south-east only. PlayerLocomotion's max step is 0.45 m, so this is a hard barrier coming back -- you walk around via the crossroads.

water.name: Water_Lake
water.note: Traced from the -2.2 m isoline of the baked height field, so the waterline cannot disagree with the ground that holds it.

water.name: Water_Stream
water.flowDirection: south from the plunge pool, across the route at the bridge, then south-east and round into the lake
water.note: Surface falls 1.70 m over 66 m. The channel is carved by the same conform pass as the roads, so the bed is always 0.5 m below the surface here.

waterfalls.name: Waterfall_Spur
waterfalls.note: Env_Waterfall_Shelf gives the lip only. The falling sheet, plunge ring and foam are shader/VFX work, not in this file.

caves.name: Cave_AsterGrotto
caves.note: A hollow inside Mass_MassifWest: subtract this volume from the massif and cap it. The chamber narrows to 6 m at the passage and opens to 18 m at the back, so the reveal happens in one step.

paths.name: Path_TownMain
paths.note: Aster Town's one street. Cobbled, 5 m, from the south gate to the north gate; it wanders by up to a metre so it is never a ruled line. The plaza is a widening of it. Forty metres end to end, which at the camera's 14 m screenful is three separate pictures rather than one; the old 29 m street was a screenful and a half and you could see the whole town from either end of it.

paths.name: Path_TownLane_West
paths.note: Back lane serving the west quarter. Half the main street's width -- two road widths is what makes a town read as having a hierarchy rather than a grid. It is a loop, leaving the street at z=-19.6 and rejoining it at z=-30.4, because a lane that dead ends is a lane you walk once: this one has the west row's four front doors on its north verges and the paddock and orchard on its outer ones, and it brings you back.

paths.name: Path_TownLane_Lab
paths.note: Short spur from the plaza up the 0.4 m step to the lab door. Runs along the camera axis -- exactly the 45 degree diagonal -- so the dome is dead ahead as you climb it. It used to run east instead and its far end was three metres inside the lab's own footprint, which the placement audit read as a nine-metre building standing in a road and duly shoved the lab off the axis the whole town is composed on. It now stops 1.2 m short of the door the emitter derives at (-5.23, -10.14).

paths.name: Path_GateRamp
paths.note: The cut through the town's retaining cliff. 2.3 m of fall over 9 m -- 14 deg, well inside the 48 deg slope limit. The height field carves this corridor, so the ramp and the cliff either side of it are the same surface.

paths.name: Path_RouteSpine
paths.note: Route 1. Four metres of worn dirt, bending twice so you never see more than about 18 m of it at once. Walled by the massif to the north-west and the ledge shelf to the south-east; the walkable band either side of it is 6-11 m of plain grass. Crosses the stream on the one bridge at (13.6, 18.2) -- that crossing is the route's gate.

paths.name: Path_CrossroadsFork
paths.note: The west arm out of the crossroads, toward the gorge. Passes the plunge pool at a respectful eight metres, which is the distance at which a waterfall reads as a view rather than as an obstacle.

paths.name: Path_CaveBranch
paths.note: Climbs the gorge between the two massifs: 3 m of rise over 22 m, steepest (16 deg) between z=33 and z=41. The walls squeeze to 9 m apart, which is the pinch that makes the cave mouth an arrival rather than a door in a field.

paths.name: Path_LakeBranch
paths.note: Crossroads to the lakeside, falling 1.7 m into the basin over 24 m. Ends on the beach a metre above the waterline, looking north-east across open water -- the one long sightline in the slice, and the payoff for the enclosed route.

paths.name: Path_LakeShoreTrail
paths.note: A two-metre desire line, not a road: the west shore trail to the lookout. Narrow enough that it reads as something walked into existence rather than built.

paths.name: Path_CaveInterior
paths.note: Worn floor through the cave: entry passage, main chamber, back alcove. Gravel, not dirt -- the material change is the only cue the player gets that they are inside.

foliageFields.name: Field_Route_NorthGrass
foliageFields.note: The big encounter field, filling the gap between the road's north edge and the massif foot. One contiguous mass with a readable silhouette -- BDSP tall grass is never a sprinkle.

foliageFields.name: Field_Route_SouthGrass
foliageFields.note: Second field, south verge. Deliberately narrower so the player can choose to skirt it -- avoidable encounters are what make the wide ones a decision.

foliageFields.name: Field_Route_ShelfGrass
foliageFields.note: On the shelf below the ledge, around the item ball. The reward for hopping down.

foliageFields.name: Field_Route_Meadow
foliageFields.note: A thin sprinkle over the whole valley floor -- roughly one tuft every 3 m, which is what Route 201 actually has. The empty ground is the point.

foliageFields.name: Field_Lake_Reeds
foliageFields.note: Reed belt on the west shore, following the waterline band between -2.2 and -1.4. Reads as the boundary between walkable and swimmable.

foliageFields.name: Field_Lake_Lilypads
foliageFields.note: On the water surface at y=-2.2, thinning toward the middle so the lake still reads as open water you would want to surf across.

foliageFields.name: Field_Lake_ShoreGrass
foliageFields.note: Beach-side encounter field, the only one in the zone -- water Pokemon come from the surf trigger instead.

foliageFields.name: Field_Lake_Meadow
foliageFields.note: Thin cover over the basin's west slope.

foliageFields.name: Field_Cave_Moss
foliageFields.note: Moss on the floor and boulder tops; the only green in the zone, so it carries the whole colour note.

foliageFields.name: Field_Cave_Grass
foliageFields.note: The chamber's encounter patch, pushed to the back so the player has to commit to the dark before anything happens.

foliageFields.name: Field_Gorge_Meadow
foliageFields.note: Damp ferny cover up the gorge floor.

foliageFields.name: Field_Town_Lawn
foliageFields.note: Kept sparse on purpose. Wedgehurst's lawns are almost bare; the eye needs somewhere to rest between the buildings.

foliageFields.name: Field_Town_WoodNorth
foliageFields.note: The north rim and the crook of the west hills. Stops 3 m short of the gate: this polygon's east end and Field_Town_WoodEast's north end are the two jambs of the town's only door.

foliageFields.name: Field_Town_WoodEast
foliageFields.note: Behind the terrace's retaining wall, from the gate down to the south-east shoulder, and round the *back* of the lab. That north-east corner used to be bare: the lab's own rear elevation looked out over the shelf at +2.73 m and straight off the rim, a 3.4 m drop to the route, which is the same 'the town just stops' reading as the street running into the horizon. The wood now stands on the shelf 10-12 m behind it -- on the flat, not on the 25-37 degree rim face, which the emitter would drop at MAX_PLANT_SLOPE anyway -- and closes to within 4 m of the east gatepost, so the treeline funnels into the gate rather than offering a second way out beside it.

foliageFields.name: Field_Town_WoodSouth
foliageFields.note: Behind the south gate and the working yard. The hillside behind it climbs from 2.7 m to 12 m in six metres, so this is the screen and the hill is the wall.

foliageFields.name: Field_Town_WoodWest
foliageFields.note: The west edge, between the lane loop's outer verge and the foot of the west hills.

foliageFields.name: Field_Town_WoodEastRidge
foliageFields.note: Beyond the rim, in the gully at the foot of the town's east cliff and up the south-east hillside behind it. Pure backdrop -- unreachable, and there so the view over the retaining wall is canopy rather than the dead flat that was there. Thinner than the walls proper because none of it is ever near the camera.

playerSpawn.name: Spawn_Player
playerSpawn.note: On the plaza's south-east corner, on the exact 45 degree camera axis to the lab: the lab is at (-1.5, -6) and this is (-1.5 - 7.5, -6 - 7.5). Moved 2.6 m back down that axis so the shot opens on the plaza rather than on the lab's doorstep, and so the market row and the well are in the same frame. The note this replaces claimed the opening frame was 'the dome filling the top of the screen'. That is not achievable and never was. The exploration camera is pitched 38 degrees down with a 40 degree vertical FOV, so the top edge of the frame is a ray leaving the camera 18 degrees BELOW horizontal: from a camera eye 5.2 m up nothing above 5.2 m is ever in shot, and it falls a further 0.33 m for every metre of distance. The lab is 9.33 m tall and its dome starts at 6 m. No ground-level position in this town can frame it. What the opening frame actually is, and what it is now composed for, is the lab's ground floor and door filling the top third with the plaza falling away below -- see the report against this pass.

healingMachine.name: Anchor_HealingMachine
healingMachine.note: Inside the Pokemon Centre's plot on the plaza's north side. It used to stand in the open street because there was no Centre to put it in; the emitter holds it back as an interior fixture, and this anchor is where Interior_PokeCentre will place it.

npcs.name: NPC_Gardener
npcs.note: In the west field behind the orchard, which is the reason the west lane has a top arm. Moved out of the plaza so the town's six residents are spread over its three streets rather than all standing in one square.

trainers.name: Trainer_Route_Youngster
trainers.note: Sight cone crosses the road from the south verge, between the two tall-grass fields. You walk into it looking at the ledge.

trainers.name: Trainer_Route_Lass
trainers.note: Faces back down the road from the north verge; catches you on the second bend, so the two route trainers never trigger together.

trainers.name: Trainer_Lake_Fisher
trainers.note: On the shore trail, facing the water; triggers as you come north off the beach.

trainers.name: Trainer_Cave_Hiker
trainers.note: Just inside the chamber where the passage opens out -- the first thing the torch light finds.

waterBodies.name: WB_Stream
waterBodies.note: Too shallow and too fast to surf; the trigger exists so the splash and footstep sets switch.

roamerSpawnRegions.name: Roam_Route_Meadow
roamerSpawnRegions.note: Pidgey, Rattata, Pikachu, Oddish -- skittish, keep to the tree line.

roamerSpawnRegions.name: Roam_StreamValley
roamerSpawnRegions.note: Water types down the stream. Reachable only across the stepping stones at (33.2, 15.6), which is the slice's one optional detour.

roamerSpawnRegions.name: Roam_Town_Yard
roamerSpawnRegions.note: Two only. A town with wildlife in it stops feeling safe. Moved to the west field beyond the orchard, which is the only part of the enlarged town that is not somebody's plot.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_Waterfall_Mist
ambientAnchors.note: The plunge pool. Mist is the near-lens layer for every shot up the fork.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_Cave_Mouth_Light
ambientAnchors.note: God ray through the arch -- the only thing separating inside from outside.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_Town_Yard
ambientAnchors.note: The working end of the street. Quieter than the plaza on purpose -- a town with one ambience everywhere is a town with one place in it.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_Plaza_Warm
ambientAnchors.note: Night only. Lifts the plaza out of the blue hour so the town still reads.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_Lab_Key
ambientAnchors.note: Grazes the lab's south-west face -- the one the fixed camera always sees.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_LampGlow_Town_Lamp_01
ambientAnchors.note: Night only. Sits at the lantern, not at the post's foot.

ambientAnchors.note: Night only. Sits at the lantern, not at the post's foot.

ambientAnchors.note: Night only. Sits at the lantern, not at the post's foot.

ambientAnchors.note: Night only. Sits at the lantern, not at the post's foot.

ambientAnchors.note: Night only. Sits at the lantern, not at the post's foot.

ambientAnchors.note: Night only. Sits at the lantern, not at the post's foot.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_TownWood_Birds_01
ambientAnchors.note: In the canopy. The boundary wood is silent geometry otherwise.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_TownWood_Birds_02
ambientAnchors.note: In the canopy. The boundary wood is silent geometry otherwise.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_TownWood_Birds_03
ambientAnchors.note: In the canopy. The boundary wood is silent geometry otherwise.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_TownWood_Birds_04
ambientAnchors.note: In the canopy. The boundary wood is silent geometry otherwise.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_TownGate_Flush
ambientAnchors.note: Birds off the gateposts as you step into the gap. The one moment of movement on the only threshold the town has.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_Market_Awnings
ambientAnchors.note: The stall canopies. Cloth that moves is the cheapest thing on the plaza that says somebody is standing under it.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_Yard_Work
ambientAnchors.note: Hammering from the yard behind the south row.

ambientAnchors.name: Amb_Centre_Sign
ambientAnchors.note: The Centre's sign over its door.

requiredAssets.name: terrain material set
requiredAssets.what: Tiling ground materials, 2048^2, quantised in place: grass_meadow, grass_short_town, dirt_route, cobble_town, flagstone, shore_sand, cave_gravel, cliff_rock_strata.
requiredAssets.why: The height field is one mesh; it needs a splat/triplanar set, not props.

requiredAssets.name: road ribbon material + edge decal
requiredAssets.what: dirt_route and cobble_town with an alpha-feathered edge (edgeBlend 0.7-1.1 m) so the generated road mesh dissolves into grass instead of ending on a line.
requiredAssets.why: Replaces the 226 paving tiles. BDSP roads have a scalloped, worn margin.

requiredAssets.name: tall grass instanced card set
requiredAssets.what: 3-4 tall-grass cards, 0.9-1.2 m, wind vertex colours, authored to read as a dense field at 1.5/m2 with GPU instancing.
requiredAssets.why: foliageFields declares ~4,900 instances; they must not be 4,900 GameObjects.

requiredAssets.name: cliff face material + strata normal
requiredAssets.what: Rock material with horizontal strata and a hard normal break, for the skirt generated between each cliff's topPolyline and basePolyline.
requiredAssets.why: Replaces the 205 modular cliff wall props, which read as a rash of boxes.

requiredAssets.name: cave interior shell
requiredAssets.what: Wall and ceiling material for the hollow described in terrain.caves, plus a mouth-arch blend so the generated shell meets Env_Cave_Arch cleanly.
requiredAssets.why: The kit has stalactites but no room to hang them in.

requiredAssets.name: water: lake + flowing stream + waterfall sheet
requiredAssets.what: PokeLabWater variants for a still lake, a flowing stream with a flow map following Water_Stream.centreline, and a falling sheet + plunge ring + foam for the 8.15 m drop.

requiredAssets.name: town gate arch or fence gate
requiredAssets.what: A 4.5 m wide gate piece for the head of Path_GateRamp.
requiredAssets.why: The town's one exit currently has a signpost and nothing else.

requiredAssets.name: wooden jetty (4-6 m)
requiredAssets.what: Small pier for the beach at (40, 33), pointing north-east into the lake.
requiredAssets.why: Gives the surf entry point a staged foreground and the fisher NPC a place.

requiredAssets.name: hedge / low wall run
requiredAssets.what: 1 m and 2 m modules of clipped hedge and dry-stone retaining wall.
requiredAssets.why: Wedgehurst bounds every plot; picket fence alone cannot carry all of it.

requiredAssets.name: ledge lip piece
requiredAssets.what: A 2 m grass-topped ledge lip with an exposed earth face, for the 1.25-1.35 m one-way ledges.
requiredAssets.why: The ledge must read as hoppable at a glance, which is a silhouette job.

requiredAssets.name: second and third house silhouettes
requiredAssets.what: Two more house shapes; six buildings on three meshes repeats visibly.
requiredAssets.why: Roof pitch and chimney position are what the eye counts in a town.
